While their advising activity in this repository is limited to 2013, they have published five articles spanning from 2014 to 2026. Robert B. Figueroa has advised one thesis in this repository, which was completed in 2013. This supervised work, titled "Implementing and Maintaining a Completely Free Solution for Hosting a Small Organization's Content-Management System," focused on the sub-topics of information systems and management and leadership. The research examined the difficulties small organizations face when transitioning from traditional information dissemination to digital platforms, using a TRC employees' cooperative as a case study. While their advising activity in this repository is limited to that single 2013 entry, Figueroa has published five articles in the repository, with the most recent work dated 2026.

Based on their published research, Figueroa's academic interests are broad and multidisciplinary. They show a significant focus on online and distance learning, which appears in three of their articles. This includes research on the feasibility of delivering team-based physical education within open and distance e-learning (ODeL) environments and trends regarding Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) in six emerging APEC member economies. Their work also touches on the crowdsourced planning and development of MOOC platforms through design thinking and hackathons.

Information systems is another recurring theme in Figueroa's work, appearing in three articles. This includes research on developing and evaluating websites as Open Educational Resources (OER) for faculty development, as well as studies involving content-management systems and platform development. Figueroa has also explored the intersection of technology and social themes, such as the BUKAS Lab, which focuses on artscience exploration and futures literacy in the Global South to address sustainable development and socioeconomic justice.

Other research areas covered by Figueroa include management and leadership, which appears in two articles, and governance and public policy, which appears in one. They have also contributed to research regarding language and literacy, specifically in the context of artscience and futures literacy. Their work spans various geographic contexts, including the Philippines, Japan, and the broader APEC region. While their thesis supervision in this repository is limited to a single student from 2013, their published body of work suggests a research profile centered on the intersection of digital information systems, online education models, and social development. Evidence regarding their specific capacity for supervising current students is thin, as their latest recorded advisee year in this repository is 2013.
